items.description:
`chcon` resolved recursive targets from `fts_accpath` with a fresh path lookup, so traversal and the SELinux get/set were not bound to traversal directory state. A privileged recursive relabel can be redirected to unintended objects under rename/symlink races. Fix opens targets with `openat` against the traversal cwd fd before the SELinux operation.

**Fixed in 0.10.0** (PR #12566, commit 7cfc74e47ffab452663be6842d788a5164d9688b): recursive relabel resolution is anchored to the traversal dirfd.

items.title: uu_env incorrectly rejects backslashes within single-quoted strings accepted by GNU env
items.description:

items.title: split: TOCTOU output-open allows truncating a swapped file
items.description:
`split` checks input/output identity by path before opening the output, then opens with truncation, leaving a race window on mutable path components. GNU opens first and compares the opened output inode against the input before truncating. The race can cause `split` to truncate/write a file different from the one validated — including the input file or another file the process can access.

**Fixed in 0.10.0** (PR #12565, commit 58040feb5c66fce588a7ffac299b3a23bd55cd81): the output open path is hardened against TOCTOU target swaps.

---

When fetching objects from a malicious repository, Git LFS may execute an arbitrary command or binary after incorrectly parsing the Git configuration options defined for a submodule.

NLTK ships a security wrapper, `nltk.pathsec.ZipFile`, that is meant to confine archive extraction to trusted data roots and to block link-based escapes. When `nltk.download()` installs a package, the extraction write opens each member's target path without checking whether that path is a hardlink to a file located outside the data root.
